title: riley-harper-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-31
content:
Scratchpad: end-to-end notes for recent regression seen on refund-classifier prompt set

Context:
- Running nightly evals (batch job ev-evals-01) against refund-classifier v2.1 (quantized) and fallback v2.0 (full-precision).
- Observed spike in false-positive rate for 'chargeback' category on 2026-03-28 nightly run (FP from 4.2% -> 12.8%).
- Customer impact: small but visible increase in erroneous refund approvals in Canary (customer: retail-pro).

Quick hypothesis list (ordered):
1) Prompt mutation (recent prompt-template tweak in PR#221) introduced leading phrase that biases toward refund.
2) Quantization path (v2.1 int8 path) mis-handling negation tokens for this template distribution.
3) Data drift: new examples in production include unusual merchant codes and terse customer notes not covered in eval set.
4) Batching-related latency/timeouts causing truncated context in streaming path (rare).

Ad-hoc rubric (for triage runs) — score each sample 0..3 and note failure mode:
- 0 = correct/acceptable (model recommendation matches ground truth label, reasoning plausible)
- 1 = minor issue (correct label but missing explanation or hedging language)
- 2 = borderline/wrong with recoverable prompt change (model misinterprets, but small prompt tweak could fix)
- 3 = clear regression (contradicts ground truth or hallucinated reason)

Sample inspection (random 50 from 2026-03-28 FP bucket):
- S1: "I didn't receive item. Please refund."  -> model: APPROVE REFUND (reason: 'not delivered')  (score 0)
- S7: "Customer used promo; charged twice? not sure." -> model: APPROVE REFUND (reason: 'duplicate charge')  (score 3)  <-- likely prompt misread: model treated 'not sure' as evidence
- S12: "Dispute: chargeback opened by cardholder, merchant says item delivered." -> model: APPROVE REFUND (score 2)  <-- needs stronger context understanding
- S21: "Fraud suspected. cardholder denies purchase." -> model: DENY REFUND (score 0)
- S33: "Merchant refunded already, but customer says still charged." -> model: APPROVE REFUND (score 3)  <-- duplicates / timing confusion

Observed patterns:
- Short, terse notes with punctuation errors often flip to APPROVE (FP).
- Mentions of 'promo'/'discount' correlate with higher FP (maybe model treats promo mentions as signals for refund).
- v2.1 quantized shows higher FP than v2.0 on same sample set (consistently ~+8% FP).

Quick experiments to run (priority order):
- Exp A (prompt-only): rollback recent template tweak from PR#221 in staging and re-run nightly subset (N=500). Measure FP delta.
- Exp B (model-path): run same N=500 on v2.0 vs v2.1 with identical prompts, batching=1 (disable continuous batching) to rule out batching truncation.
- Exp C (tokenization): compare tokenization/byte-level diffs for teres/typo samples between v2.0 and v2.1 quantized pipeline.
- Exp D (data augmentation): add 200 synthetic terse negative examples ("not sure", "maybe", "promo") to eval set and re-run evaluation.

Immediate temp mitigation (canary safety knobs):
- Add a route-level fallback: if model confidence < 0.6 and output==APPROVE, route to v2.0 or human review.
- Add a post-processing rule: if output==APPROVE and text contains 'promo' or 'discount' and doesn't include explicit delivery failure tokens, downgrade to HUMAN_REVIEW.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Run Exp A and Exp B on subset today (target: 150 samples each) and update JIRA-7642 with results.
- [ ] Check PR#221 diff for leading phrases and replicate locally. (Maya to help)
- [ ] Ask infra to pull quantization logs for v2.1 (timestamp range 2026-03-27..2026-03-29). (Sam)
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing note if spike confirmed and customer-facing impact found (ops@).
- [ ] Add synthetic terses to eval corpus and schedule re-run for nightly full job.

Quick snippets / commands used:
- export SAMPLESET=~/evals/refund/2026-03-28_fp_sample.json
- python evals/run_batch.py --model v2.1 --input $SAMPLESET --out out_v21.json --batch-size 1 --disable-streaming
- python evals/compare.py out_v21.json out_v20.json --metrics fp_rate precision recall --diff > diffs_03_28.txt

Slack threads / refs:
- see slack thread: #evals "refund spike" (ts=1700779200) for initial alert
- Confluence draft: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=84532 (refund classifier incident notes)
- JIRA: JIRA-7642 (triage + experiments)

Open questions:
- Is this truly quantization-related or an emergent prompt-distribution issue? Need token-level debug.
- Do we have telemetry on per-token logits for quantized runtime? If not, ask infra to add quick debug endpoint.

End: will iterate after running Exp A/B. Keep this doc as living scratchpad.

-- Riley H.
